subject: Post-call: Streaming & SLO measurement — alignment + next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Cho <emma.cho@averysys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Streaming & SLO measurement — alignment + next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the intro call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment going into the qualification run: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Streaming/response-level SLOs: target p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms for single-turn streaming for your 1.5k token average responses.
- Throughput: sustained 15–25 requests/sec per model shard; occasional bursts to 60 rps for peak batch windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency per endpoint ~40 users, spike up to 120 for the US region.
- Functional constraints: partial streaming with early-stop tokens; client expects SSE-like events and consistent per-chunk latencies.
- Quality: baseline acceptance with your rubric (recall/precision numbers) — you said you’ll share the seed prompt set.

Proposed benchmark scope (short):
1) Reproducible harness run using our benchmark template (attached). We’ll run: cold-start 50 parallel streams (to measure prefix latency), steady-state 25 rps for 30 minutes (throughput), and a burst test to 120 concurrent streams for 5 minutes.
2) Measurement definitions: p50/p95 token-emit latency, end-to-end response time, throughput (req/sec successful), token-generation/sec on GPU, and drop/failure rates.
3) Artifacts for handoff: your prompt set (v1), our benchmark config, and a shared results sheet.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Emma/David: please attach the prompt set + your acceptance rubric (seed examples) so we can map scoring to our harness fields. (Deliverable: avery_prompt_set_v1.json)
- Internal: Karthik & Marcus to prepare a config that targets your p50/p95, and validate streaming emitter hooks in the harness.
- Timeline: proposed run next Tue 2026-07-13 (US morning) — if that works we’ll reserve Dedicated capacity for the run.

I’ve attached the benchmark template and a starter SLO spreadsheet to this thread. Will loop in Billing/Legal separately if we need trial credits for reserved capacity.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_template.md (markdown), avery_slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Cho <emma.cho@averysys.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Streaming & SLO measurement — alignment + next steps

Thanks Priya — I sketched a draft harness config and a short checklist. Key technical notes we should confirm with Avery before the run: 

1) Tokenization / model parity: which model variant do they want us to run? They mentioned an open Llama-like model (7B q8) in the call but also referenced a proprietary finetune. We need a binary decision: use "model-7b-q8" or "avery-finetune-v1" for parity. Implication: quantization and kernel paths change latency profile.

2) Streaming semantics: their client expects chunked events every ~50 tokens (approx). I recommend we measure both per-chunk p50/p95 and per-response finalization time. The harness can emit chunk timestamps.

3) Concurrency driver: I’ll wire the harness to a k8s job that spins up synthetic clients from two AZs to mimic cross-AZ latencies. We should confirm their expected client-to-region RTT (they said ~35–60ms).

Checklist (short):
- [ ] Prompt set ingested into harness (format: JSONL, each item with id, prompt, expected fields).
- [ ] SLO sheet mapped to metrics names (p50_token_emit_ms, p95_token_emit_ms, end_to_end_ms, success_rate)
- [ ] Run window confirmed (start/end times)
- [ ] Reserved capacity confirmed (if Dedicated)

Marcus: I’ll assign you the streaming hooks task; can you produce a quick runbook for interpreting per-chunk QoS anomalies?

-karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Cho <emma.cho@averysys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Ruiz <david.ruiz@averysys.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Streaming & SLO measurement — alignment + next steps

Thanks all — this looks great. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Model: we have an internal finetune (avery-deploy-1) but are ok running the open 7B quantized variant for the first pass to baseline infra performance. We will share the finetune artifact if performance looks good.
- Prompt set: attached avery_prompt_set_v1.json (contains 120 seed prompts across your 3 buckets: short, medium, long outputs).
- Acceptance rubric: we’ll use a simple scale (0/1) for correctness + a noise-tolerance check; I attached the rubric sheet as well.
- Scheduling: Tue 2026-07-13 09:00 PT is fine. Please lock the slot and confirm if you need a specific region or GPU flavor.

One ask: can you include token-enqueue metrics so we can see whether observed latency is due to queuing vs compute? It’ll help us decide whether to increase instance count vs change batching.

—Emma
Director, ML Platform — Avery Systems
emma.cho@averysys.com | +1 617-555-0233

All — quick status update ahead of Tuesday’s run and a few operational notes: 

Status:
- Harness: config baked from the template and prompt set ingested (see attached redwood_benchmark_template.md references in the drive link).
- Metrics: added token_enqueue_ms and executor_ms to the collection pipeline; we’ll tag metrics by client-AZ to separate network vs compute.
- Model: running baseline passes on model-7b-q8; we’ll snapshot kernel selection and quant flags into the run metadata for reproducibility.

Operational asks (for the run):
- Priya: please confirm whether we should reserve Dedicated capacity (NVIDIA T4 pool) — if so we need approval from Sales Ops for a trial credit.
- Emma: confirm whether bursts should be simulated from a single region or two regions (you mentioned US-only but sometimes NYC clients bounce through EU infra).

Deliverables we will produce after the run:
1) Raw run artifacts (logs, per-chunk timestamps, raw metrics) — pushed to the Drive folder.
2) A short-run analysis doc with SLO pass/fail, root cause notes for any p95 regressions, and suggested knob changes (batch size, cache policy, shard count).
3) Repro script (how to re-run the same harness with exact seed/config).

We’re on track for 07/13 09:00 PT — I’ll create the run ticket and tag everyone.

-marcus
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Reliability — Redwood Inference
